Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

psychnets 0.6.2

Documentation

  • Vignettes rechecked against current output. The Ising and mixed graphical model vignettes described networks from an earlier release (7 edges and a self-regulation to test-anxiety edge); their prose now matches the current fits (6 edges, test anxiety isolated under the AND rule; the OR rule adds the negative edge). Each vignette shows the edge table with as.data.frame(), which summary() returns only invisibly, and lists its method references.
  • Examples no longer reach into result objects with $: certificates are read with certificate(), stability with print(), and the certificate helpers (glasso_kkt(), ggm_support_kkt(), glm_lasso_kkt()) are shown on exact closed-form optima. panel_gvar() examples use the bundled srl_panel; Ising examples use dichotomize(SRL_GPT). Every print method has an example.
  • Method references added to the estimator, centrality, predictability and resampling help pages; DESCRIPTION references now give authors and years.

psychnets 0.6.1

Complete function-review fixes

  • Case-dropping stability now counts undefined correlations and failed fits against the requested certainty, rather than inflating stability by omitting those draws. Two-node edge-reliability diagnostics return available deviation metrics with an unavailable correlation instead of failing.
  • Resampling preserves source-column identities when custom labels and ignored nonnumeric columns are present. Grouped diagnostics forward explicit estimator options, composite grouping keys cannot pool distinct tuples, and groups of within/between models can be printed and summarized.
  • Event-feature missingness follows the requested handling instead of deleting an otherwise varying feature. Within-person centering uses available values per variable. Generic independent-row resampling and NCT now refuse repeated- person event groups: reconstructing these as cross-sectional samples had lost their effective sample size and could change even the observed graph.
  • Panel models refuse missing person identifiers, support empty EBIC networks in all accessors and plots, return CFI = 1 when both estimated noncentralities are zero, and match edge significance without ambiguous label concatenation. Plot abbreviations override defaults, custom line styles no longer carry a misleading significance key, and nlambda must be a finite whole integer.
  • Kendall marginal-network significance uses a tie-corrected Kendall test. Kendall significance without raw data, or for full-order partial correlations, is refused rather than applying Pearson p-values. Polyserial estimates are invariant to the numeric spacing of ordinal codes.
  • MGM automatic predictability uses raw-scale Gaussian observations. Public prediction preserves original source columns independently of display labels, applies the training category encoding to numeric and factor inputs alike, and refuses unseen categories.
  • Wald-pruned IsingSampler fits retain their pre-pruning score as fit_kkt and report the altered network’s certificate as unavailable. Covariance PSD validation runs in correlation units, including for relative-importance fits.
  • Two-node external Ising/MGM fits work through an inert design-padding column; moderation requires at least three nodes. TMFG certificates now also validate planar stacked-triangulation structure.
  • Small-world null rewiring randomizes undirected edge orientations and retains rejected proposals, removing node-order restrictions and accepted-move bias. NCT plots identify signed global expected influence when abs = FALSE.

Review fixes

  • Panel EBIC path diagnostics now recompute the objective and KKT residual after small coefficients are rounded to zero. Infeasible rounded candidates are excluded from selection instead of retaining a stale certificate.
  • ebic_glasso(refit = "unregularized") now uses the same confirmed lambda and support as the default penalized fit before the unpenalized refit.
  • Glasso’s returned ebic_path includes the rescored EBIC values, so its minimum agrees with the selected lambda and reported EBIC.
  • Panel plots accept overrides such as node_fill, layout, title, and edge colours through ... without duplicate-argument errors.

New estimator: panel graphical VAR

  • panel_gvar() estimates the panel graphical vector-autoregressive model (Epskamp 2020) from few-wave, many-person panel data: a directed temporal network (within-person lag-1 effects), a contemporaneous network (partial correlations of the within-person innovations), and a between-person network (partial correlations of the stable person means). The within-person process is a stationary VAR(1) around a random intercept with stationary means – the model of psychonetrics::panelgvar() – fitted by maximum likelihood in base R (nlminb with an analytic reverse-mode gradient, then a Fisher-scoring polish). Long data (vars, id, wave) or wide data (vars as a variables-by-waves design matrix) are accepted.
  • Robust on raw-scale, small-sample data: the optimizer works on standardized variables (an exact reparameterization – the model is scale-equivariant) from three deterministic starts (moment-based, neutral, and the fitted baseline), keeps the best, and refuses (psychnet_no_converge error) to return a fit worse than its nested baseline. On weekly means of an experience-sampling panel (41 persons, 0-100 scales) this reaches a lower objective than psychonetrics on every design compared, where a single unscaled start had diverged.
  • plot() draws the three networks side by side on one shared circle layout, with the temporal autoregressive effects as self-loops, edge weight labels, solid (significant) vs dashed (not) edges, blue positive / vermillion negative (Okabe-Ito), and “no edges” on an empty network.
  • as.data.frame(fit, what = "variance"): per-variable split of the implied variance into the between-person and stationary within-person parts (an intraclass correlation, share_between).
  • New dataset srl_panel: a synthetic panel of 100 students x 4 weeks on five self-regulated-learning indicators (0-100), simulated once from a panel-GVAR whose structure was taken from real experience-sampling data (the anonymized esm_srl data of the idiographic package). New vignette “Panel graphical VAR: temporal, contemporaneous, and between-person networks” works through it.
  • standardize = c("none", "z", "z_per_wave"), as psychonetrics’ panelvar(standardize =): "z_per_wave" z-scores every variable within every wave, removing drift in wave means and variances (matches psychonetrics’ chi-square to three decimals).
  • Penalized EBIC selection, select = "ebic" – the panel counterpart of ebic_glasso() and psychonetrics’ panelgvar(estimator = "PML"): lasso on every temporal (autoregressions included), contemporaneous and between parameter, 50-value lambda path from lambda_max with warm starts, EBIC (gamma = 0.5), optional unpenalized refit. Accelerated proximal gradient that never leaves the model’s domain, then an active-set Newton polish; certified by the lasso KKT conditions (~1e-10); the selected lambda is re-solved from three starts and their agreement reported. Matches psychonetrics’ PML on every simulated design compared (same lambda, same zero pattern, estimates within 3e-3, lower penalized objective); on weekly ESM means psychonetrics’ PML returns an invalid model (non-positive-definite contemporaneous block) while select = "ebic" returns a certified one. Lasso estimates carry no p-values (significant is NA; the plot draws selected edges solid).
  • Robustness (from an adversarial review): the EBIC choice is reconsidered after the final certified solve (a final solve can change a lambda’s EBIC; the path table marks fully solved rows in final); only variances on the optimizer’s actual bound are treated as active constraints (a near-zero but interior variance no longer has its score suppressed in the certificate); singular-information SEs use the pseudo-inverse on the identifiable eigenspace (dropping unidentified coordinates had understated the SEs of parameters conditioned on their identifiable combinations); all post-fit computation runs on the standardized scale, so data whose variables differ in units by orders of magnitude (or are tiny) fit identically instead of failing a covariance check or crashing in a data-scale solve.
  • Edge selection is one argument, select = c("none", "prune", "ebic") (replacing the earlier logical prune).
  • Default output is the full model: prune = FALSE by default (the psychonetrics default, where prune() is a separate step). Every edge is reported with its SE, p-value, Wald CI and a new significant column (p < alpha); print() and summary() count significant edges per network, and plot() draws significant edges solid and non-significant ones dashed (sign by colour plus the signed weight label, with a line-type key). select = "prune" runs prune + step-up.
  • Step-up search after pruning (stepup = TRUE, the default when pruning; criterion = c("bic", "none")), equal to psychonetrics::stepup(): re-add the pruned edge with the largest modification index while it is significant, passes a chi-square difference test, and lowers BIC. One-pass pruning alone can remove parameters that substitute for each other (an autoregression and correlated cross-lagged effects): on weekly ESM means it removed 22 parameters that were jointly significant (chi-square 76.9, p = 5e-8), and step-up restores the two that matter. Modification indices match psychonetrics’ (score test, n g^2 / (4 V) with the Schur-complement information); the selected supports match psychonetrics’ prune() and prune() |> stepup() on every well-identified design compared. stepup = FALSE reproduces prune() alone.
  • Variances estimated at zero (Heywood cases) are treated as active bound constraints: left out of the information (their SE is NA, the others keep valid SEs) and certified by the bound KKT condition. A fit whose information is singular is pruned with infinite standard errors for the parameters it does not identify (rather than a pseudo-inverse, which would understate them). Boundary warnings now name the part on (or heading for) the boundary, e.g. “between-person variance of V2 at zero”.
  • as.data.frame(fit, what = "diagnostics"): one row with persons, waves, the ML score certificate, boundary flag, SE availability, and how many of the three starts reached the best optimum (fewer than three = competing local optima).
  • Pruning follows psychonetrics::prune(): Wald p-values from the expected Fisher information, alpha = 0.01, optional adjust (any p.adjust method) and recursive; prune = FALSE returns the saturated fit.
  • Self-certified: the ML score on the free parameters is recomputed by a forward-mode Jacobian (independent of the optimizer’s reverse-mode gradient) and reported by print(); it is ~1e-13 on the validation designs.
  • Validated against psychonetrics 0.17.8 on three designs (3 x 4, 5 x 5, and a BH-adjusted n = 150 case): identical pruned support in every case, and psychonetrics’ own fit function rates the psychnets estimate as the deeper optimum (its default optimizer stops with a gradient near 1e-3, which moves estimates by up to ~1e-3). Fit indices (chi-square, CFI, TLI, RMSEA, AIC, BIC) agree to that tolerance.
  • Read the fit with as.data.frame(fit) (edges with SE, p, Wald CI), as.data.frame(fit, what = "parameters"), as.data.frame(fit, what = "fit"), or as.data.frame(fit, what = "diagnostics"). The object is a netobject_group, so plot() / cograph::splot() draws the three networks as a grid.
  • Classed conditions: psychnet_bad_input errors (fewer than three waves, too few persons, na_method = "pairwise", …), and psychnet_boundary, psychnet_singular_information, psychnet_listwise_drop, psychnet_no_converge warnings. A near-singular contemporaneous or between covariance (partial correlations near +/-1, common with three waves) is flagged rather than reported silently.
  • Missing data: listwise only. Full-information ML (psychonetrics’ default when data have missing values) is not yet implemented, and a pairwise covariance is refused because it is not a likelihood for this model.
  • net_crosswalk("panelgvar") maps the psychonetrics arguments.
  • No existing estimator’s numbers changed; the new golden baseline lives in a separate fixture (golden-panelgvar.rds).

ebic_glasso(): absent edges are exact zeros

  • An edge the EBIC selection counted as absent could be returned in $weights as a floating-point residue of about 1e-17 instead of 0 (the $edges table already dropped it). This happened when the selected lambda sat at max|S_ij| (the empty graph) after the positive-definite projection, and in a substantial share of sparse fits generally (10 of 40 random n = 60, p = 12 null draws in the new regression test). Anything that compares weights with zero read the residue as an edge; in net_compare() two empty networks gave M = S = 5.6e-17 and a false p = 0.02 instead of 1 (found by the NetworkComparisonTest parity grid). Precision entries with |theta_ij| <= 1e-10 – the same rule the EBIC uses to count edges – are now returned as exact zeros, so the network has exactly the support the EBIC scored. Every edge above 1e-10 is unchanged; the golden baselines pass at 1e-12. Because the returned support can change (residue -> 0), this ships in the 0.6.0 minor release per the numerical-stability policy.

ebic_glasso(): the selected lambda is the exact EBIC minimum

  • The lambda path is scanned at a loose tolerance (1e-4) and only the chosen lambda was refit tightly. The scan can leave an entry that is zero at the optimum just above the 1e-10 edge-count threshold; one miscounted edge raises that lambda’s EBIC by exactly log(n) + 4 gamma log(p) and can hide the true minimum. The NetworkComparisonTest parity audit found this in 4 of 29 divergent fits (EBIC up to 9.6 units worse than the optimum). Every lambda whose scan EBIC is within two edge penalties of the best is now refit at the refit tolerance and rescored, and the lowest exact EBIC wins. On the audited fits psychnets now reaches the lower exact EBIC in 29 of 29 (NCT/qgraph in 4, because qgraph counts a ~1e-17 residue as an edge at lambda = max|S_ij| and so never selects an empty graph). Default engine only; engine = "glasso" is unchanged. About 40% more time per fit; golden baselines, equivalence and every estimator suite pass unchanged.

Network comparison test (net_compare()) fixes

  • BREAKING – the M and S letters were the wrong way round. In van Borkulo et al. (2022) and NetworkComparisonTest, M is the network-structure test (largest absolute edge difference) and S the global-strength test; psychnets printed and stored them swapped, so a write-up copied from print() reported the wrong statistic. The tests are now stored as $structure (M) and $strength (S); reading the old $M / $S raises a psychnet_renamed error that says which field to use, rather than silently returning the other test. Printed and tabled labels use the NCT letters. $strength$by_group (shown by print()) holds each network’s global strength, NCT’s glstrinv.sep; with abs = FALSE the test is labelled global expected influence, as in NCT.

On complete data every returned number is unchanged (frozen in tests/testthat/fixtures/nct-baseline.rds), and under a shared seed the M, S and per-edge p-values equal NetworkComparisonTest::NCT() 2.2.2 exactly.

  • Missing values no longer erase a variable. A single NA made every correlation of that variable NA, which was then replaced by 0, so the variable lost all its edges in the observed networks and in every permutation, with no warning. New na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise") (default "pairwise", as for the estimators): pairwise correlations with the median co-observation count as the sample size; listwise drops incomplete rows (whole pairs in a paired design).
  • A constant variable now enters the network as an isolated node through an explicit rule (the convention of every psychnets estimator for a constant column) instead of a blanket NA -> 0 replacement under suppressWarnings(); a constant variable in an observed group raises a psychnet_constant_variable warning. A variable that becomes constant in a permuted split (a rare binary item) is handled the same way, so the statistic is defined on every split and the test stays exact.
  • With pairwise missing data, a variable pair sharing fewer than two observed rows (in a group or a permuted split) has an undefined correlation and is refused with psychnet_degenerate_sample instead of being set to 0.
  • Columns that differ in name or order raise psychnet_bad_input (unchanged rule, now a classed condition with the offending names).
  • Group mode (net_compare(psychnet(d, group = "g"))) forwards the group’s gamma and na_method, and warns (psychnet_estimator_mismatch) when the group was built with a non-glasso method, a threshold, or other estimator settings: the networks compared are then EBIC-glasso networks, not the group’s own.
  • Argument validation: iter must be a single whole number (2.7 was truncated, "10" was accepted); malformed arguments raise psychnet_bad_input.
  • Printing the result shows everything: the two groups by name (the argument names, or the group levels in group mode), M and S with each group’s global strength, the number of differing edges, and every edge (largest difference first) with both groups’ weights, rounded p-values and * for p < 0.05 (print(fit, n = 10) shortens the edge list). As tables, summary() gives the M and S tests and as.data.frame() one row per edge (from, to, weight_1, weight_2, difference, p_value, significant).
  • plot(type = "edges") marks significant edges with * as well as colour.

psychnets 0.5.2

CRAN release: 2026-08-23

CRAN incoming-check runtime

  • Resubmission addressing the automated incoming pre-test NOTE (12 examples over 10 s and an overall checktime over 10 min on the Windows builder). No estimator numerics changed.
  • Resampling examples (net_boot(), difference_test(), net_stability(), net_casedrop_reliability(), net_split_reliability(), and their plot methods) now demonstrate the workflow with the closed-form method = "pcor" estimator and note that the "glasso" default with full iteration counts is what a real analysis should use. net_compare() examples use fewer permutations on smaller data.
  • The cograph visualization vignette’s bootstrap chunk uses method = "pcor".
  • Four heavyweight numerical test files are skipped on CRAN (they run on every GitHub Actions matrix job, R-hub platform, and local devtools::test()); the frozen 1e-12 golden estimator baselines still run on CRAN.

psychnets 0.5.1

Pre-release correctness hardening

  • The base nodewise kernel (ising_fit(), mgm_fit(), moderated MGM with native = TRUE) now returns exact zeros for inactive lasso coordinates. Coordinate descent could leave a BLAS-rounding crumb (~1e-17) on a coordinate whose gradient sits exactly at the penalty boundary; whether the crumb was 0.0 or 4e-17 differed between BLAS implementations, and the AND rule then counted it as an edge on some platforms but not others. The EBIC degrees of freedom already ignored such coefficients (|beta| <= 1e-10); the returned support now agrees. One golden-fixture edge changes: the base-kernel mixed-data mgm network loses a spurious weak edge, matching the glmnet reference path, which always reported that edge as absent.
  • cor_auto() now rejects variable pairs with fewer than two joint observations instead of optimizing an empty polychoric likelihood. Marginal-correlation p-values use pair-specific effective sample sizes; full-order partial-correlation inference rejects heterogeneous pairwise sample sizes.
  • Bootstrap, stability, case-drop, and split-half refits retain the observed node set when a resample makes a node constant. Failed-fit counts are exposed, invalid small-sample splits are rejected, and estimator_args carries estimator options whose names collide with diagnostic options. The legacy net_boot(engine=) argument is translated to the public native switch.
  • Bootstrap difference tests split exact ties between both tails, so identical draw distributions return p = 1.
  • Corrected undirected node-betweenness normalization, preserved directedness in relative-importance aggregation, and prevented rank dichotomization from splitting tied values by row order.
  • Certificates that are unavailable, including post-threshold GGM graphs and conditioned moderated networks, now report certified = NA. GGM objects retain the pre-threshold residual in $fit_kkt.
  • The glmnet Ising/MGM paths and moderated MGM now honor nlambda and lambda_min_ratio; moderated MGM honors both LW and HW. MGM consistently stores $levels, and prediction accepts original two-level factor columns.
  • GGM predictability now uses the fitted marginal variance when the precision diagonal is penalized.

Unblocks Nestimate’s delegation of its cross-sectional psychometric estimators to psychnets (see AGENT-NOTE-NESTIMATE-DELEGATION.md, gaps A and B). Default numeric output of every estimator is unchanged; all new behaviour is opt-in. Two functions are renamed — see below.

BREAKING: two reliability verbs renamed

  • casedrop_reliability() is now net_casedrop_reliability().
  • network_reliability() is now net_split_reliability().

The old names are removed, not deprecated. Both were also exported by Nestimate with a different first argument (a fitted network there, raw data here), so library() load order silently decided which one a user got and the failure surfaced as an argument-matching error inside their own code. Nestimate is the older package and now depends on psychnets, so psychnets is the side that renames. An erroring alias would not have fixed anything — psychnets would still own the name and still shadow Nestimate’s verb.

Neither the arguments, the return value, nor the numbers changed; only the name. Update calls with a search and replace. The new names also bring both verbs into the net_* style every other framework verb already uses.

net_edge_betweenness() is not renamed: both packages give it the same contract, so it is genuinely one verb rather than a collision.

ebic_glasso() can now serve a resampling caller

  • New lambda_path = argument: scan a caller-supplied penalty grid, in the order given, instead of recomputing one from the input correlation matrix. Resampling callers compute the path once from the original matrix and reuse it for every resample, so selected penalties stay comparable across draws rather than drifting with each sample’s largest absolute correlation.

  • New penalize_diagonal = argument (default FALSE, unchanged behaviour). glasso_kkt() gained a matching argument: with a penalized diagonal the optimality condition becomes W_ii = S_ii + rho, so grading such a fit with the default would report a spurious violation of exactly rho. Verified against the glasso Fortran package to ~1e-11.

  • New refit = argument. TRUE (default) keeps today’s behaviour of re-solving the selected penalty to machine precision. FALSE returns the path fit exactly as scanned – a bit-compatibility switch for consumers holding frozen baselines against an unrefitted path scan, not a performance knob. "unregularized" keeps the selected support and refits the unpenalized graph-restricted MLE on it, certified by ggm_support_kkt() instead of glasso_kkt(). $support is stored on the object in that case only.

mgm_fit() supports multi-level categorical nodes

  • mgm_fit(native = FALSE) now models a factor/character column, or a numeric column with more than two levels, as a single k-level categorical node. Previously these errored, and the suggested workaround (one-hot encoding) was not equivalent: it turns one k-level node into k separate nodes, a different model. Matches mgm::mgm() to ~1e-15 with exact structure on 3- and 4-level factors.

  • Node type detection now follows mgm::mgm()’s own rule: a factor/character column is categorical, and so is a numeric column with 10 or fewer distinct integer values. A numeric column promoted by that integer rule is warned about by name (condition class psychnet_type_promotion), because it switches the node from gaussian to categorical – a different model, not a different encoding. Likert and count items hit this rule routinely. No previously-working call changes its result: every input newly classified as categorical raised an error before, and constant / all-NA columns are still dropped as before. A character column with more than 10 distinct values is refused as an identifier (use factor() to insist), and a column declared "c" via types = with more than 10 distinct values is refused as a mislabelled continuous variable rather than routed to a multinomial.

  • na_method applies identically on both engines: the glmnet path is fed the same imputed (or listwise-reduced) rows as the base path, and a missing multi-level code is imputed with the modal level rather than a mean.

  • The certificate of a multi-level node is the multinomial (softmax) stationarity residual. Grading each class as an independent logistic regression reported ~0.2 for a fit glmnet had converged; the true residual is ~1e-5. Related: on the glmnet paths (mgm_fit / ising_fit, native = FALSE) a node whose EBIC-selected model is empty now certifies as optimal (residual ~0) instead of reporting its whole gradient as a violation – the empty solution is exact at glmnet’s own lambda_max. Only $kkt changes; weights are untouched.

  • The resampling verbs (net_boot(), net_stability(), net_casedrop_reliability(), net_split_reliability()) now hand each draw to the estimator exactly as the full data would be: a data.frame keeps its factor columns and its incomplete rows, a matrix is coerced without dropping rows. So resampling mgm_fit(native = FALSE) keeps a factor node (previously it was silently dropped), and na_method = "pairwise" – every estimator’s default – resamples the rows a direct call would use instead of a listwise-reduced subset (previously the verbs listwise-deleted up front, so the bootstrapped network was not the network psychnet() returns on the same data). Node labels are read off the observed fit. For method = "mgm" node types are decided once on the full data and pinned via types= for every draw, so a borderline column cannot flip between gaussian and categorical from draw to draw, and the promotion warning is raised once per verb call. Complete numeric data is byte-identical to before.

  • mgm_fit(): constant / all-NA columns are dropped before anything is indexed against the columns, and moderators (a positional index) and a labels vector given for all original columns now follow that drop; a moderator that is itself constant is refused by name. na_method = "listwise" is applied first, so a node left with one level after deletion is dropped like any other constant column on both engines. An explicit factor with more than 10 levels is accepted (that is the documented escape hatch); only character columns and types = "c" declarations on non-factor columns are subject to the 10-level guard.

  • A 2-level column is recoded through its factor levels, so any binary coding ({1,2}, {"no","yes"}) now works and gives the same fit as {0,1}.

  • The base kernel (native = TRUE) is a binomial solver and still refuses a node with more than two levels, now naming the column and pointing at native = FALSE.

  • net_predict() refuses an mgm network containing a multi-level categorical node: a k-level predictor occupies k-1 design columns, so there is no one-coefficient-per-variable matrix to predict from. It errors rather than computing from a truncated model.

Documentation and stability

  • Node order is now a documented guarantee, not observed behaviour: $weights, $nodes, and $precision follow the input column order and are never sorted. Stated in ?ebic_glasso, ?cor_network, ?pcor_network, ?mgm_fit and pinned by a test using non-alphabetical names.

  • A numerical-stability policy is now documented: estimator numerics are stable within a minor version; any change to a selected support, or to a weight beyond 1e-10, ships in a minor bump and is listed here. Enforced by tests/testthat/test-golden.R against frozen fixtures at 1e-12, so downstream consumers can pin psychnets (>= x.y) against the promise.

  • net_crosswalk() gained rows for penalize.diagonal, refit, and lambda_path, which it previously listed as reference-only.

psychnets 0.4.3

CRAN release: 2026-07-30

  • First CRAN release.

  • mgm_fit(..., moderators = ) (the moderated mixed graphical model, read with condition()) now runs on psychnets’ own base-R penalized-IRLS kernel and is KKT-certified. It previously required the compiled glmnet package and silently ignored native =. Every estimator in the package is now pure base R by default; glmnet and glasso remain optional reference engines selected with native = FALSE.

  • The base moderated kernel covers gaussian and binary nodes (the documented mgm_fit() scope) and errors explicitly on a categorical node with more than two levels, which needs native = FALSE.

  • The two resampling-heavy long-form guides, “Network reliability” and “Visualizing networks”, are now website articles rather than installed vignettes, so they keep their full iteration counts while the package check stays inside CRAN’s time budget. Read them at https://pak.dynasite.org/psychnets. The eight remaining vignettes are unchanged and still ship with the package.
